Ibn al-Anbari said: its meaning is among those righteous in state with Allah. al-Kirmani said: the prophets were singled out for mention of righteousness because no opposite of that intrudes upon their righteousness. al-Zajjaj said: the righteous is one who performs what is obligatory upon him and the rights of people towards them, end quote.

Sulayman said, after prophethood had been granted to him: ﴿And admit me by Your mercy among Your righteous servants﴾ [al-Naml: 19]. It has been said: the realization of this is that the prophets have a measure of righteousness, which if diminished, prophethood would be negated; then after they share in that measure, their ranks vary in the increase above that measure, so whoever has the greater share of righteousness has the higher rank. al-Maturidi said: righteousness is realized in every prophet in all respects, while in others it is realized only in some of them; and although the name applies to all, the reason for the name being deserved by the prophets is the realization of righteousness in all respects, while in others it is in some of them. So He specified it by mention, so that the possibility of prophethood being permissible in general believers is cut off; thus restricting it by the name of righteousness was beneficial. It has also been said: among the righteous in this world and the Hereafter, so it is an indication of persistence in faith and security from fear of the bad end.

﴿He said: My Lord, how can I have a son when old age has overtaken me and my wife is barren?﴾ His previous request to his Lord had preceded: ﴿My Lord, grant me from Yourself good offspring﴾ [Al Imran: 38]. There is no doubt about the possibility and permissibility of that; and if it was possible, and the angels gave him good news of it, what is the purpose of this question?

It has been answered in several ways. One: that it is a question about the manner, and the meaning is: will a child be born to me at the age of old age and with my wife being barren? That is, she has reached the age of one who does not bear children; he had reached ninety-nine years, and his wife had reached ninety-eight years. Ibn Abbas said: he was one hundred and twenty when he was given the good news; al-Kalbi said: he was ninety-two years old.

Or: shall I and my wife be restored to the age of youth and the state of one who has children? It was answered: he will be given a child in this state. This meaning was said by al-Hasan and al-Asamm. The second: that when he was given the good news of a child, he sought to know: would that child be from his own loins or from his sons?

The third: that he had forgotten the question, and between the question and the announcement there were forty years; and it is narrated from Sufyan that between them there were sixty years. The fourth: that this inquiry was by way of magnifying the power of Allah the Exalted; it occurs upon witnessing the signs, and its meaning comes back to what some said: that it was from intense joy, for he was like one astonished when what he was accustomed to considering impossible came to pass. The fifth: he only asked because he was incapable of intercourse due to his old age, so he asked his Lord: will He strengthen him for intercourse, and will his wife accept it in her state of old age? The sixth: he asked whether the child would be granted from his barren wife, or from another.

The seventh: that when he was given the good news of a child, Satan came to him to cloud the blessing of his Lord for him, and said to him: Do you know who called you? He said: The angels of my Lord. He said: No, it was that Satan; and if this were from your Lord, He would have concealed it from you as you concealed your call. So a whisper mixed with his heart, and he said: ﴿How can I have a son?﴾ so that Allah would make clear to him that it was from revelation. This was said by Ikrimah and al-Suddi. The judge said: if the speech of the angel were confused for the speech of Satan to the messengers, the trust in all the laws would not remain.

It is answered: what he said does not follow, because it is possible that a miracle establishes the revelation regarding matters of religion, while matters pertaining to the worldly interests may not be confirmed by a miracle, so the possibility remains, and he seeks its removal. al-Zamakhshari said: it is a remote inference from the standpoint of custom, just as Maryam said. End quote. But according to what he said: if it were a remote inference, he would not have asked it by saying: ﴿grant me from Yourself good offspring﴾ [Al Imran: 38], for one does not ask except for what is possible, especially prophets, since breaking custom for them occurs frequently.

And: "yakun" may be a complete verb with "ghulam" as its subject, meaning: how will a boy come to be born to me? It may also be a defective (incomplete) verb, and in that case the predicate does not necessarily have to precede the subject, because it has been said: the entry of kana makes valid the beginning with an indefinite noun, since the preceding of the interrogative particle justifies beginning with an indefinite noun. The two clauses after each of them are circumstantial (hal), and the governing element in both is "yakun" if it is complete, or the governing element in "li" if it is defective.

It has been said: "wa-imra'ati 'aqir" is a circumstantial clause of the object in "balaghani," and the governing element is "balaghani." The first clause was verbal because old age renews itself little by little, so it was not an inherent description; and the second was nominal with the predicate "'aqir," because her being barren is a necessary matter for her and not an accidental attribute, so it was fitting that the first be a verbal clause and that the second be a nominal clause. The meaning of "balaghani al-kibar" is: it affected me. The real meaning of reaching is in physical bodies, namely that the one who reaches moves to the place reached.

He attributed the reaching to old age as a broadening of speech, as though old age were seeking him, since events befall a person, so they are as though seeking him, and he is the one sought. It has been said: it is of the inverted kind, as came: ﴿and I have indeed reached from old age a withering﴾ [Maryam: 8], and as the poet said:
"Like the hedgehogs, scuttling, they have reached Najran, or their private parts have reached Hajar."

al-Raghib said: when you reach old age, old age has reached you, end quote. Here he put his own condition first and delayed his wife's condition, whereas in Maryam he reversed this. al-Maturidi said: the wording is not observed in narration; rather the meanings contained in the wording are observed. Others said: the opening of the verses in Maryam conforms to this order here, for there he mentioned that the bone had weakened in him, ﴿and the head glistened with grey hair﴾ [Maryam: 4]. And he said: ﴿and indeed I feared my successors after me, and my wife has been barren﴾ [Maryam: 5]; so when he repeated her mention in the inquiry, he delayed the mention of old age so that "itiyya" would match the rhyme endings, and this is a principle sought in eloquence, preferred when it does not impair the meaning. The conjunction here is "wa," so the placing first and last does not indicate a precedence in time; rather this is from the category of placing first what fits better in the eloquence of speech.

﴿He said: Thus Allah does what He wills.﴾ The kaf is for comparison, and "dhalika" refers to the act, that is: like that act, which is the formation of a child between one who has aged and a barren woman. Allah does what He wills of strange acts; so this is a report from Allah that He does the things to which His will relates as an act like that act; nothing can frustrate Him, and the cause of its existence is the attachment of His will, whether it be among the acts that follow custom or among those that do not follow custom.

(p-451) Since Allah (exalted is He) brings things into existence from pure non-existence, without material or cause, how much more so for things that have a material and a cause, even if that is contrary to the custom? In this case, the kaf (ka, "like") occupies a position of accusative (naṣb) as an attribute (ṣifah) of a deleted verbal noun (maṣdar), meaning: an act like that act; or it occupies the position of a circumstantial qualifier (ḥāl) from the pronoun of the deleted maṣdar in "yafʿalu" (he does). This is according to the view of Sibawayh, and a similar matter has already been mentioned by us. It is also possible that "kadhalika Allah" is a subject and predicate (mubtada' and khabar), with a deleted modifier (muḍāf) in between, meaning: the wondrous handiwork of Allah is like that handiwork. In this case, "yafʿalu ma yashā'" is an explanation (sharḥ) of the ambiguity (ibhām) in the demonstrative (ism al-ishārah). Al-Zamakhshari estimated it, in a similar manner to this attribute, as: Allah. He said: "(yafʿalu ma yashā')" is an elucidation (bayān) of it, i.e., He does what He wills of the acts that break customary norms, end quote.

Ibn ʿAtiyyah said: That is, like this wondrous power, the power of Allah is [the same]. End quote. According to this possibility, the kaf is in the position of nominative (rafʿ), because the prepositional phrase and its object are in the position of the predicate of the subject, and the statement consists of two clauses. According to the first interpretation, the statement is one single clause.

Ibn ʿAtiyyah and others said, and the wording is Ibn ʿAtiyyah's: It is possible that the demonstrative "bi-dhalika" refers to the condition of Zakariyya and the condition of his wife, as if he said: "My Lord, in what manner will we have a boy, while we are in such a state?" So He said to him: "Just as you are, a boy will be born to you." The statement is complete according to this interpretation at His saying "kadhalika," and His saying "Allah does what He wills" is a clause that explains and firmly establishes in the soul the occurrence of this wondrous matter, end quote of his words. Thus "kadhalika" is related to a deleted element. Al-Raghib explained the meaning, saying: He grants you a son while you are in your state.

The apparent view among these three opinions is the first.

Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 3, verse 41:

﴿He said, "My Lord, appoint for me a sign." He said, "Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three days except by gestures."﴾ Al-Rabi', al-Suddi, and others said: Zakariyya said, "My Lord, if that address is from You, and the glad tidings are true, then appoint for me a sign, a mark by which I may know the soundness of that." So he was punished for this doubt concerning the command of Allah by being prevented from speaking with the people for three days. But a group of the exegetes (mufassirun) said: Zakariyya never doubted at all; he only asked about the manner in which the child would come, and by which the glad tidings would be completed. When it was said to him, ﴿Thus Allah does what He wills﴾ [Al 'Imran: 40], he asked for a sign of the time of conception, so that he would know when the conception of Yahya would take place.

They differed over his being prevented from speaking: was it due to an affliction that befell him, or not due to an affliction? Jubayr ibn Nufayr said: his tongue swelled in his mouth until it filled it, then Allah released him after three days. Al-Rabi' and others said: Allah seized his tongue so that he was unable to speak, as a punishment for asking for a sign after the angels had spoken to him directly with the glad tidings. And a group said: it was not an affliction, but he was prevented from mingling with people, so he was not able to do so, while he was able to mention Allah. This is what al-Tabari said, and he related something similar from Muhammad ibn Ka'b. The sign was the restraint of the tongue, so that the period would be devoted to the remembrance of Allah, his tongue not occupied with anything else, out of eagerness to fulfil the due of that great blessing and to give thanks for it. It is as if, when he asked for the sign for the sake of thanks, it was said to him: "Your sign is that your tongue be restrained except from giving thanks." The best and most fitting answer is that which is derived from the question and drawn out of it. The miraculous element in this verse lies in his ability to mention Allah and his inability to speak to people, along with the soundness of his body and the balance of his temperament; and also in the occurrence of the conception and its taking place in accordance with the reports. It was also said: he was commanded to fast three days, and they used not to speak during their fasting. Abu Muslim said: it may be that its meaning is: "Your sign is that you will be commanded not to speak to the creation, and to occupy yourself with remembrance in gratitude for the granting of this gift; and when you are commanded to that, the sought-for thing will have been achieved." It was said: so he asked Allah to impose on him an obligation which he would make a means of thanks for that.

What the apparent meaning of the verse indicates is that he asked for a sign showing that a son would be born to him, and He answered him that his sign is the absence of speech from him with the people for three days except by gesture, and he was commanded to remember and glorify (Allah). The absence of speech may be due to something voluntarily undertaken, or to its necessary consequence in their law, namely fasting; and it may be due to a compulsory prevention for a specific period, caused by an affliction in the organ, or without affliction. They said: while he retained the ability to speak by mentioning Allah. Al-Zamakhshari said: "For this reason He said: ﴿and remember your Lord﴾ to the end," meaning: during the days of your inability to speak to people; and it is one of the striking signs. End of quotation.

What he said is not to be taken as definitive, because of the possibilities we have mentioned concerning the ways in which the absence may be understood; and because the command to remember and glorify is not restricted to the time in which he does not speak to people; and even if that is restricted, it is not necessary that the remembrance and glorification be by spoken words. The apparent meaning of "appoint" (ij'al) here is "make," so it takes two objects: the first is "a sign," and the second is the prepositional phrase preceding it, namely "li" ("for me"). It is necessary that this be placed first, because before the verb "appoint" it is what permits beginning with an indefinite noun. Ibn Abi 'Abla read: an la tukallima, with the mim in the nominative, taking "an" as the light form of the heavy ("anna"), meaning "that he will not speak," its noun being omitted, the pronoun of the matter (damir al-sha'n); or treating "an" as operating like the verbal "ma." The accusative of "thalatha ayyam" is adverbial (zarf), contrary to the Kufans, who claimed that the time-noun is wholly covered by the action, so it is not an adverb, but takes the accusative like a direct object, as in "samata yawman" ("he kept silent a day"). Thus the accusative of "thalatha ayyam" is, in their view, as an object, because the absence of speech from him to the people was occurring throughout all three days, no part of them being free of that absence. The intended meaning is three days with their nights; this is shown by his saying in Surat Maryam: ﴿Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three nights while sound﴾ [Maryam: 10]. This weakens the interpretation of those who said: he was commanded to fast three days, and they did not speak during their fasting, since nights are far from being legislated for fasting; and it does not specify the beginning of the three days, but says simply "three days." If that was by way of obligation, it may be left to his choice, so that he refrains from speaking to the people for three days whenever he wishes; and it may be from the moment of the address. If it was by compulsory prevention, then it appears that it is from the moment of the address.

It was said: in this there is evidence of the abrogation of the Qur'an by the Sunnah, on the assumption that Zakariyya was able to speak during those three days, and that his law is our law; and that it was abrogated by his saying ﷺ: "There is no silence for a day until night." Many scholars have held that its meaning is: "There is no silence of a day," i.e., from the remembrance of Allah; as for silence from what has no benefit in it, that is commendable.

As for the exception of the gesture (ramz): it was said that it is a disjunctive exception (istithna' munqati'), since the gesture does not fall under speech, for whoever applied the word "kalam" in the language to a sign indicating what is in the mind of the one who signals, it is not far that this be a connected exception according to his view. For this reason the grammarians recited:

"She wanted to speak, but she feared her watcher, so there was nothing but a signal with the eyebrows."

And another said:

"When she addresses me with languid eyes, I answer her with bursting tears."

The later poets (muwallidun) used this meaning. Habib said:

"She spoke to him with eyelids that do not speak, so the reply was what his chamberlain said."

That it is a connected exception was begun by al-Zamakhshari, who said: when it performs the function of speech, and what is understood from it is understood, it is called speech. As for Ibn 'Atiyya, he preferred that it be disjunctive, saying: the speech intended in the verse is only utterance with the tongue, not informing about what is in the soul; so the real character of this exception is that it is disjunctive; and he began with this first, saying "the exception of the gesture, which is a disjunctive exception." Then he said: the jurists regarding signs and the like held that they have the status of speech in matters of oaths and the like; on this view the exception is connected. The gesture here is a movement of the two lips, said by Mujahid; or a sign with the hand and head, said by al-Dahhak, al-Suddi and 'Abd Allah ibn Kathir; or a sign with the hand, said by al-Hasan; or an indication, said by Qatada. The indication is a sign, but he did not specify with what he indicated. It is related from Qatada: a sign with the hand or a sign with the eye; this is related from al-Hasan.

It was also said: his gesture was writing on the ground. It was said: a sign with the index finger. It was said: with the tongue. From this is the poet's line:

"For days he remained, gesturing the words from his age, not dumb."

It was also said: the gesture is a faint sound. 'Alqama ibn Qays and Yahya ibn Wathhab read: rumuzan, with damma on the ra' and the mim; this is explained as the plural of rumuz, like rusul and rasul; or as a verbal noun of the pattern "rumz," the eye following the fa' as in "al-yusr" and "al-yusur."

Al-A'mash read: ramazan, with fatha on the ra' and the mim; this is explained as the plural of rami, like khadim and khadam; and its accusative when it is plural is as a circumstantial state (hal) of the doer, which is the pronoun in "tukallima," and of the object, which is "al-nas," as the poet said:

"If I meet you alone, you will surely know which of us is the knight of the factions."

That is: except making signs to one another, just as the mute speaks to people and they speak to him. In His saying ﴿except by gesture﴾ there is evidence that signing takes the place of speech, and this is found in many places of the Sunnah. In a hadith: "Where is Allah?" She pointed with her head to the sky, and he said: "Free her, for she is a believer." Thus Islam was validated by gesture, and this is the root of the religion which preserves blood, protects property and admits to Paradise; so gesture is general across all religions, and this is the view of most jurists.

﴿And remember your Lord much﴾ It was said: the remembrance here is in the heart, since he was prevented from speech; and it was said: it is with the tongue, since he was prevented from speaking with people, but was not prevented from remembrance. It was also said: it is by omission of a noun, meaning: remember the bounty of your Lord and His answer to your supplication. Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: if anyone were permitted to abandon remembrance, Zakariyya would have been permitted, and the man in battle. Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿When you meet a company, stand firm, and remember Allah much﴾ [al-Anfal: 45], and He commanded much remembrance so that the remembrance of Allah for him would increase through His blessings and graces, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So remember Me, I will remember you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 152].

"Much" (kathiran) is in the accusative either as an adjective of an omitted verbal noun, or as a state (hal) from the pronoun of the omitted verbal noun indicated by "udhkuru," according to the view of Sibawayh.

﴿And glorify with the evening and the morning﴾ That is: declare Allah free from the marks of deficiency by uttering with the tongue, saying "Subhan Allah." It was said: the meaning of "wa sabbih" is "and pray." From this: he used to pray the forenoon prayer (subha al-duha) four units; had it not been that he was among those who glorify (Allah) in one of the two senses. The apparent meaning is that he was commanded to glorify Allah at these two times: the beginning of dawn, and the time when the sun inclines toward setting; this was said by Mujahid. Others said: it may be that by "al-'ashiyy" he meant the night and by "al-ibkar" the day, expressing with a part of each of them the whole, which is a fine metaphor. The object of "wa sabbih" is omitted because it is known, since before it is: ﴿And remember your Lord much﴾, meaning: and glorify your Lord. The "ba'" in "bil-'ashiyy" is locative, that is, "in the evening."

It was read irregularly: wal-abkari, with fatha on the hamza; this is the plural of bakar with fatha on the ba' and the kaf. You say: "I came to you bakaran" (early in the morning), and it is of a kind that is obligatorily adverbial when it refers to a specific day; its counterpart is sahar and asjar, jabal and ajbal. This reading is suitable to "al-'ashiyy" according to the view of those who took it as the plural of 'ashiyya, since in it there is a correspondence in plurality; and it is likewise suitable when "al-'ashiyy" is singular and the alif and lam in it are generic, as in His saying ﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss﴾ [al-'Asr: 2], and "the yellow dinar has ruined people."

As for the reading of the majority: wal-ibkari, with kasra on the hamza, it is a verbal noun, so it has matched "al-'ashiyy" which is a time-noun with a verbal noun, and so requires an omission, that is: "in the evening, and at the time of the morning." The apparent sense of "al-'ashiyy" and "al-ibkar" is that the alif and lam in both are generic, and it is not meant the evening of those three days, nor the time of the morning in them. Al-Raghib said: the glorification does not mean only the two ends of the day, but continuing worship throughout these days. Others said: that the intended glorification is prayer is indicated by the mention of the evening and the morning; it is as though He said: remember your Lord throughout all these days and nights, and pray at the two ends of the day. End of quotation.

"Bil-'ashiyy" is connected to "wa sabbih," and this is the second verb's operation, which is preferable; for if it were connected to "wadhkur rabbaka," the pronoun would have to be supplied in the second, since its omission is not permitted except in necessity. It was said: or in rare speech. It is possible that this is not a case of operation at all, so that the command to remember is not restricted to these two times.

It was said: this verse contains, among the varieties of eloquence, several types: the addition of letters in the structure in His saying "hunalika," whose benefit I have already mentioned; repetition, in "rabbihi" ("qala rabbi"), in "inna Allaha yubashshiruka," in "bi-kalimatin min Allah," in "a'ya" ("ayatuka") in "yakunu li ghulam," and in "kanat" with the feminine form of the masculine by agreement with the wording; and "dhurriyyatan tayyibatan"; the metaphorical attribution in "wa qad balaghani al-kibar"; and the question and answer: "qala rabbi anna? Qala kadhalika," "qala rabbi aj'al li ayatan," "qala ayatuka."

The masters of the craft said: the best of this type is that in which the qalqalah (echoing sounds) abounds, and omission occurs in several places.

Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 3, verses 42–43 (part 1 of 2):

﴿And when the angels said: "O Mary, indeed Allah has chosen you, purified you, and chosen you above the women of the worlds."﴾ ﴿"O Mary, be devoutly obedient to your Lord, prostrate yourself, and bow with those who bow."﴾ ﴿That is from the news of the unseen which We reveal to you. You were not with them when they cast their pens (to see) which of them would take charge of Mary, nor were you with them when they disputed.﴾ [Al 'Imran: 44] ﴿When the angels said: "O Mary, indeed Allah gives you good tidings of a word from Him, whose name is the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary, honoured in this world and the Hereafter, and of those brought near (to Allah).﴾ [Al 'Imran: 45] ﴿He will speak to people in the cradle and in maturity, and (he will be) of the righteous.﴾ [Al 'Imran: 46] ﴿She said: "My Lord, how can I have a child when no man has touched me?" He said: "So (it will be). Allah creates what He wills. When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, 'Be,' and it is.﴾ [Al 'Imran: 47] ﴿And He will teach him the Book, wisdom, the Torah, and the Gospel.﴾ [Al 'Imran: 48] ﴿And (he will be) a messenger to the Children of Israel: "I have come to you with a sign from your Lord: I will create for you from clay the likeness of a bird, then breathe into it and it will become a bird by Allah's permission. I will heal the blind and the leper, and I will bring the dead to life by Allah's permission. And I will tell you what you eat and what you store in your houses. Indeed, in that is a sign for you, if you are believers.﴾ [Al 'Imran: 49] ﴿And (I come) confirming what is before me of the Torah, and to make lawful for you some of what was forbidden to you. I have come to you with a sign from your Lord, so fear Allah and obey me.﴾ [Al 'Imran: 50] ﴿Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is a straight path.﴾ [Al 'Imran: 51]

Al-qalam (the pen): well known, and it is that with which one writes. Its plural is aqlam. The word also applies to the lot-arrow with which one casts lots, and it is a verb in the sense of a passive participle, because it is trimmed (yuqallamu), i.e., sharpened and made even. It was said that it is derived from al-qulamah, which is a weak plant because of its thinness. Al-qulamah is also what falls from the fingernail when it is trimmed, and qallamtu azfarahu means I took from them and made them even. Zuhayr said:

*Near a lion, armed, fierce, whose mane is thick, whose claws have not been trimmed.*

And one of the later poets said:

*He is likened to the crescent moon, and that is a deficiency; the paring of his fingernail is like the crescent.*

Al-wahy (revelation): the placing of a meaning into the soul in a hidden manner. It may come through an angel to the messengers, through inspiration as in His saying: ﴿And your Lord inspired the bee﴾ [al-Nahl: 68], through gesture, as in the saying of the poet:

*They conveyed to us, and the fingertips were their messengers.*

And ﴿So he inspired them to glorify (Allah)﴾ [Maryam: 11], and through writing. Zuhayr said:

*Their poems reached the non-Arabs and the horizons, remaining as revelation remains in the deaf stone.*

Al-wahy also means a written book. He said:

*So the streams of al-Rayyan, its traces have been effaced, its emptiness, as its writings preserve them.*

It was said that al-wuhiy is the plural of wahy. As for the verb, it is said awha and wahā.

Al-Masih (the Messiah): a Hebrew word that was Arabized. Its origin in Hebrew is mashiha, with a shin, and it was Arabized with a sin, just as it was changed in Musha, so it became Musa. This is what Abu 'Ubayd said. Al-Zamakhshari said: its meaning is "the blessed," like His saying: ﴿And He made me blessed wherever I may be﴾ [Maryam: 31]. It is among the honourable titles, like al-Siddiq and al-Faruq. End of quote. It was also said that al-Masih is Arabic, and there is disagreement: is it derived from al-siyahah (wandering), so that its pattern is mif'il, or from al-mash (wiping), so that its pattern is fa'il? And does it mean "passive" or "active"? There is a difference of opinion. The reason he was given this name will become clear in the exegesis.

Al-kahl (the middle-aged man): the one who has reached the age of kuhulah, the last of which is sixty. It was also said fifty, and it was said fifty-two. Then he enters the age of old age (shaykhukhah).

There is disagreement about its beginning. It was said thirty, it was said thirty-two, it was said thirty-three, it was said thirty-five, and it was said forty years.

It is from iktahala al-nabat, when the plant became strong and grew high, and from it comes al-kahil (the shoulder-top). Ibn Faris said: iktahala al-rajul and the grey hair covered him, from their saying iktahalat al-rawdah when the blossom covered it. A woman is called kahilah. End of quote.

It is related from the scholars regarding the order of the ages of a child and the changes of his conditions: while in the womb he is janin; when born he is walid; if he does not complete the first week he is sadid; if he continues to nurse he is rada'i; when weaned he is fatim; if he does not nurse he is jahush; when he crawls and grows he is darij; when his milk teeth fall out he is mathghur; when they grow again after falling he is mutaghgbar, with ta' and tha'. When he exceeds ten he is mutara'ri' and nashi'; when he is about to reach puberty he is yafi' and muhriq; when he has a wet dream he is mahzur. In all these states he is a ghulam. When his moustache turns green and his sideburns flow, he is baqil; when he becomes dhaqin (his beard grows), he is fata and sharikh; when his beard is complete he is mujtama'. Then, as long as he is between thirty and forty, he is shabb; then he is kahl until he completes sixty. This is what is well known among the people of lexicography.

Al-tin (clay): well known. It is said tanahu Allahu 'ala kadha, and tamahu, by replacing the nun with a mim, meaning He created and formed him in such a way. Mutayyan is a title of a well-known hadith scholar.

Al-hay'ah (form): the shape and the image. Its origin is a verbal noun. It is said: haa al-shay' yahay'u hay'an and hay'ah, when a thing is arranged and settled into some state. It is transitive by doubling, so you say hayya'tuhu. He said: ﴿And (He) will prepare for you﴾ [al-Kahf: 16].

Al-nafkh (blowing): well known.

Al-ibra' (healing): the removal of illness and disease. It is said: bari'a al-rajul and bara'a min al-maradh (the man was healed of the illness). As for (being free) from sin or from religion, one says bari'.

Al-akmah: blindness that a person is born with, and it may also occur later. It is said kamaha yukimmuhu kamahan, so he is akmah. And kammahtuha: I made her blind. Suwayd said:

*I blinded his eyes until they became white.*

And Ru'bah said:

*She turned away from her, like the turning away of the blind.*

Al-baras: a well-known disease, which is whiteness that afflicts the skin. From it one says baras, so he is abras. The moon is called abras because of its whiteness, and the lizard is a poisonous abras because of the whiteness that covers its skin.

Dhakhara: he dhakharahu, kept it hidden. Al-dhukhr is what is stored. He said:

*For it are the mouse-like rats of meat which it fattens, from the wild cats and a store of its rabbits.*

﴿And when the angels said: "O Mary, indeed Allah has chosen you"﴾: When he had finished the story of Zakariyya, and had digressed from the story of Mary to Zakariyya's, he returned to the story of Mary. This is the usual manner of Arab speech: when they mention something, they digress from it to something else, then return to the first if they have a purpose in returning to it. The aim is to clear Mary of what the Jews accused her of, and to show that it is impossible for Jesus to be a god, so he mentions his birth. The apparent meaning of his words "the angels" is that they are a group of angels. It was also said that what is meant is Gabriel and those with him of the angels, because it is reported that he does not descend for a matter except with a group of angels. It was also said that it was Gabriel alone.

Ibn Mas'ud and Abdullah ibn 'Amr read: "wa-idh qala al-malaikatu" (and the angels said). In the angels' calling her by her name there is reassurance for her and preparation for what they are about to tell her. The object of the verb "said" is the sentence emphasised with inna (indeed).

The apparent meaning is that the angels addressed her directly with speech. Al-Zamakhshari said: It is reported that they spoke to her directly, miraculously, as a sign for Zakariyya, or as a foreshadowing of the prophethood of Jesus. End of quote. By "foreshadowing" he means a precursor and an indication of the prophethood of Jesus. This is the position of the Mu'tazilah, because according to them a supernatural event (khariq li-l-'adah) does not occur at the hand of one who is not a prophet, unless there is a prophet in his time or one is awaited, so that such an event is a preface before the sending of that prophet.

﴿And purified you﴾: purification here means from menstruation, as Ibn 'Abbas said. Al-Suddi said: Mary did not menstruate. Some people said: from menstruation and postpartum bleeding. It is related from Ibn 'Abbas: from the touch of men. And from Mujahid: from whatever blemishes women in form, character, and religion. And from him also: from doubts and suspicions.

﴿and chosen you above the women of the worlds﴾: It was said: He repeated it for emphasis and exaggeration. It was said: there is no emphasis, because by the first choosing is meant the choosing for guardianship, and by the second the choosing for the birth of Jesus, because by his birth she gained additional choosing and a high station above her equals. It was also said: the first choosing is selection, and general, including righteous women; and the second is a choosing above the women of the worlds.

It was said: when the first choosing was stated without restriction, the second clarified that she was chosen above women, not above men. Al-Zamakhshari said: He chose you first when He accepted you from your mother and raised you, and singled you out with a noble honour, and purified you from what is detestable in acts, and from what the Jews accused you of. And He chose you last above the women of the worlds by granting you Jesus without a father, which was not given to any other woman. End of quote. This is a good statement, and "the women of the worlds" is then taken generally. The matter for which she was chosen is her singling out for the birth of Jesus. It was said that it is the service of the house (of worship). It was said: liberation (dedication), and no female was liberated except Mary. It was said: her protection from the prick of Satan. It was said: her prophethood, for it was said that she was made a prophetess, and the angels would appear to her and address her with Allah's message to her, and Zakariyya would hear that, and say: "Indeed, Mary has a great matter." But the majority hold that no woman was made a prophetess. So the meaning for which Mary was chosen above the women of the worlds is something specific to her, so it is a special choosing, since its cause is special. It was said: "the women of the worlds" is specific to the women of the world of her time, so the choosing in that case would be general, as said by Ibn Jurayj.

It is related from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "The best of the women of Paradise is Mary, daughter of 'Imran." It is also related: "The best of her women is Mary, daughter of 'Imran." It is related: "The best of the women of the worlds are four: Mary, daughter of 'Imran; Asiya, daughter of Muzahim, the wife of Pharaoh; Khadijah, daughter of Khuwaylid; and Fatimah, daughter of Muhammad." It is related: "Khadijah has been preferred over the women of my ummah as Mary has been preferred over the women of the worlds." It is related: "Indeed she is among the perfect women." It is related in the authentic hadiths the preference of Mary over the women of the worlds, and a group of exegetes went to the apparent meaning of this preference. Some of our shaykhs said: What I have seen among those upon whom the scholars have agreed is that they transmit from their teachers that Fatimah is the best of women, both the earlier and the later, because she is a part of the Messenger of Allah.

﴿O Mary, be devoutly obedient to your Lord﴾: There is no disagreement among the exegetes that the one who addressed her with this was the angels mentioned earlier, according to the difference mentioned. By qunut here is meant worship, as said by al-Hasan and Qatadah. Or: prolonged standing in prayer, as said by Mujahid, Ibn Juraij, and al-Rabi'. Or: obedience. Or: sincerity, as said by Ibn Jubayr. In His saying "to your Lord" there is an indication that you should single Him out for worship and dedicate worship to Him. The majority hold what Mujahid said, and it is the most appropriate in meaning to His saying ﴿prostrate yourself and bow﴾. Mujahid related that when she was addressed with this, she stood until her feet swelled. Al-Awza'i said: she stood until blood and pus flowed from her feet. It is also related that birds would land on her head, thinking her an inanimate object, because of her stillness in long standing.

﴿prostrate yourself, and bow with those who bow﴾: The angels commanded her to perform three of the postures of prayer. If the apparent postures are meant, then they are conjoined with "and" (wa), and "wa" does not indicate order. So one would only ask why prostration was placed before bowing from the perspective of rhetoric (ilm al-bayan). The answer: since prostration is the posture in which the servant is nearest to Allah, it was given precedence, even though in action it comes after bowing. Thus the precedence is one of honour. It was said that prostration came before bowing in the law of Zakariyya and others among them, mentioned by Abu Musa al-Dimashqi. It was said: in all religions except the religion of Islam, so the precedence came from the order of occurrence in that law, and the precedence in that case is temporal from the perspective of occurrence. This precedence is one of the five types mentioned by the rhetoricians (al-bayaniyyun), and so is the precedence that precedes it. Al-Zamakhshari and Ibn 'Atiyyah agreed that the apparent postures are not what is meant.

Al-Zamakhshari said: She was commanded to perform prayer, and qunut and sujud were mentioned because they are among the forms and pillars of prayer. Then it was said to her, ﴿And bow with those who bow﴾. The meaning is: let your prayer be with the worshippers, that is, in congregation. That is, join yourself to the body of worshippers, be with them and among their number, and do not be among the number of others.

Ibn 'Atiyya said: In my view, Maryam was commanded with two actions and two of the markers (ma'alim) of prayer, namely prolonged standing (qiyam) and prostration (sujud). These two were singled out for mention because of their status among the pillars of prayer. These two apply to her prayer when performed alone. Otherwise, one who prays behind an imam is not told, "Prolong your standing." Afterwards she was commanded to pray in congregation, and it was said to her, ﴿And bow with those who bow﴾. Here another marker of prayer is intended, so that a word is not repeated. The verse does not refer to the sujud and ruku' that are contained within a single rak'ah. The end of his words.

There is no necessity to take the wording out of its apparent meaning.

We have mentioned a reason for placing sujud before ruku'. Ibn 'Atiyya found this problematic and said: This verse is more problematic than our saying, "Zayd and 'Amr stood up," because the standing of Zayd and 'Amr has no known order, whereas it is known that sujud comes after ruku'. How then does the conjunction (waw) come in the reverse order in this verse? The end of his words.

This is the speech of one who has not looked carefully into the book of Sibawayh. Sibawayh mentioned that the conjunctive waw in coordination may carry the sense of togetherness (ma'iyyah), and that mentioning the earlier before the later, or the later before the earlier, are equally possible. Neither of the two possibilities is preferred over the other. No attention is to be paid to the view of some of our later companions who preferred togetherness over mentioning the earlier first, or over mentioning the later first, or who preferred mentioning the earlier over the later.

Al-Zamakhshari gave another explanation for placing ruku' after sujud. He said: It is possible that in her time there were those who would stand and prostrate in their prayer but would not bow, and there were those who would bow. So she was commanded to bow with those who bow, and not to be with those who do not bow. The end of his words. It is as if it was said: Do not limit yourself to standing and prostration, but add ruku' to that.

It was also said: What is meant by "qunti" is "obey," and by "usjudi" is "pray." From this is the verse ﴿And at the adbar of the prostrations﴾ [Qaf: 40], meaning the prayers. By "irka'i" is meant "give thanks with those who give thanks." From this is the verse ﴿And he fell down bowing and turned in repentance﴾ [Sad: 24]. This meaning is strengthened, and it refutes the claim of one who thinks that no prayer was legislated except that ruku' in it precedes sujud. The observed prayer of the Jews and Christians is free of ruku'. It is unlikely that ruku' means the bending that leads to sujud. It is also possible that the omission of ruku' is among what the Jews and Christians changed from the markers of their law.

In His words ﴿with those who bow﴾, the word ma'a (with) implies companionship and joint performance of ruku' together with those who bow, so she would be commanded to pray in congregation. It is also possible that ma'a is used figuratively, so it denotes only agreement in the action without actual joint performance, meaning: act as they act, even if you do not perform the prayer with them, for she used to pray in her sanctuary (mihrab). The phrase is ﴿with those who bow﴾ and not ﴿with those who bow (feminine)﴾, because this plural form is more general, as it includes men and women by way of taghlib (the masculine being used to include the feminine). It also fits the endings of the verses before and after it. And because following men is more excellent, if we say she was commanded to pray in congregation.

Al-Maturidi said: Praying in congregation was not disliked for her, even though she was young, because they were her relatives and kin, and for this reason they were specially entrusted with her care and custody. The end of his words.

﴿That is among the reports of the unseen which We reveal to you﴾ [Al 'Imran: 44]. The reference (dhalika) is to what preceded of the stories of the wife of 'Imran, her daughter Maryam, Zakariyya, and Yahya. The meaning is that the arrival of these stories to you is by way of revelation, since you were not one who studied the scriptures, nor did you accompany anyone who knew such things, and you are from an unlettered people. So the means of knowing this is only revelation from God, as He said in the other verse. He also mentioned the story of the person most distant in time from the time of the Prophet (ﷺ), namely Nuh, peace be upon him, and He gave it in full in Surah Hud more than in other places: ﴿These are among the reports of the unseen which We reveal to you. Neither you nor your people knew them before this﴾ [Hud: 49]. In this is proof of the prophethood of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), since he reported unseen matters that no one could know except one who witnessed them, or one who read them in earlier scriptures, or one to whom God revealed them. Since direct witnessing and reading are excluded, the third possibility is determined, which is revelation from God Most High.

The kaf in dhalika and ilayka is an address to the Prophet (ﷺ). The better parsing (i'rab) is that dhalika is the subject (mubtada'), and "min anba' al-ghayb" (among the reports of the unseen) is its predicate (khabar). Another option is that nuhihi is a new independent clause (jumlah mustaanifah), and the pronoun in nuhihi refers to al-ghayb, meaning: Our practice is that We reveal the unseen to you and inform you of it. For this reason the present tense is used. This is more beneficial than taking it as referring to dhalika, since it includes the stories mentioned and others that He will reveal to him in the future. It becomes like the expression "Zayd feeds the poor," which indicates a continuous state. The form used for this meaning is indeed the present tense. Whereas if it refers to dhalika, it would necessarily mean that nuhihi is in the sense of awhaynahu ilayka (We revealed it to you), since the revelation of it has already occurred and concluded. Then it would be further removed from metaphor than if it included these stories and others that will come later. They also allowed that nuhihi could be the predicate of dhalika, with min anba' being a circumstantial phrase (hal) from the ha' in nuhihi, or being related to nuhihi.

﴿And you were not with them when they cast their pens, [to see] which of them would take charge of Maryam﴾ [Al 'Imran: 44]. This is an affirmation and confirmation that what he knew of this was only through revelation from God Most High. What is being informed about is two stories: the story of Maryam and the story of Zakariyya. He drew attention to the story of Maryam, since it is the primary subject of the report, while the story of Zakariyya came incidentally, as part of it is included in the mention of who would take charge of her. So there is no omission of a reference to one of the stories.

The meaning of ﴿And you were not with them﴾ [Al 'Imran: 44] is: you were not present with them in their presence when they cast their pens. Direct witnessing is negated, although it is already negated by knowledge. The negation does not extend to reading and receiving from the preservers of reports. This is by way of mockery toward those who deny revelation, since they know that he was not one who reads or transmits from the memorizers of reports. Therefore it is determined that his knowledge of this came by revelation from God Most High to him. A parallel to this in the story of Musa is: ﴿And you were not on the western side﴾ [Al-Qasas: 44], ﴿And you were not on the side of Mount Tur﴾ [Al-Qasas: 46]. And in the story of Yusuf: ﴿And you were not with them when they agreed upon their plan﴾ [Yusuf: 102].

The pronoun in ladayhim refers not to something previously mentioned but to what the meaning indicates, that is: you were not with the disputants, like His words ﴿and raised thereby a cloud of dust﴾ [Al-'Adiyat: 4], meaning: by the place. The governing element (al-'amil) of idh is the governing element of ladayhim. Abu 'Ali al-Farisi said: The governing element of idh is "kunta" (you were). The end of his words. This does not fit his view on the incomplete kana (kana al-naqisah), since he holds that it has removed the indication of an event and become purely temporal, and what is of this nature cannot govern a time adverb, because the time adverb is a container for an event, and where there is no event it cannot govern. The present tense after idh has the sense of the past, meaning: when they cast their pens for drawing lots over Maryam. The apparent meaning is that these are the pens used for writing. It was said: They used to write the Torah with them, so they chose them for the lottery seeking blessing through them. It was also said: The "aqlam" here means the "azlam," which are arrows used for divination (al-qidah). Casting here means throwing and dropping. The verse does not mention into what they cast them, nor the manner of the casting, nor how Zakariyya's pen came out. We have mentioned previously some of what the exegetes said about this, and God knows best which of these is correct. Abu Muslim said: The nations used to write their names on arrows during disputes, and whoever's arrow came out was given the matter. This is similar to the arrows by which the slaughtered camel is divided.

﴿Which of them would take charge of Maryam﴾ [Al 'Imran: 44] is in the nominative case as the subject (mubtada'), and its predicate is in a place of accusative (nasb) either by way of quoting a verb of saying that is omitted, meaning: they say, "Which of them will take charge?" The omitted element is indicated by ﴿they cast their pens﴾ [Al 'Imran: 44]. This verse has been cited as evidence for the validity of the lottery (qur'ah), which is a legal question discussed in the science of jurisprudence (fiqh).

Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 3, verses 42–43 (part 1 of 2):

﴿And when the angels said: "O Mary, indeed Allah has chosen you, purified you, and chosen you above the women of the worlds."﴾ ﴿"O Mary, be devoutly obedient to your Lord, prostrate yourself, and bow with those who bow."﴾ ﴿That is from the news of the unseen which We reveal to you. You were not with them when they cast their pens (to see) which of them would take charge of Mary, nor were you with them when they disputed.﴾ [Al 'Imran: 44] ﴿When the angels said: "O Mary, indeed Allah gives you good tidings of a word from Him, whose name is the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary, honoured in this world and the Hereafter, and of those brought near (to Allah).﴾ [Al 'Imran: 45] ﴿He will speak to people in the cradle and in maturity, and (he will be) of the righteous.﴾ [Al 'Imran: 46] ﴿She said: "My Lord, how can I have a child when no man has touched me?" He said: "So (it will be). Allah creates what He wills. When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, 'Be,' and it is.﴾ [Al 'Imran: 47] ﴿And He will teach him the Book, wisdom, the Torah, and the Gospel.﴾ [Al 'Imran: 48] ﴿And (he will be) a messenger to the Children of Israel: "I have come to you with a sign from your Lord: I will create for you from clay the likeness of a bird, then breathe into it and it will become a bird by Allah's permission. I will heal the blind and the leper, and I will bring the dead to life by Allah's permission. And I will tell you what you eat and what you store in your houses. Indeed, in that is a sign for you, if you are believers.﴾ [Al 'Imran: 49] ﴿And (I come) confirming what is before me of the Torah, and to make lawful for you some of what was forbidden to you. I have come to you with a sign from your Lord, so fear Allah and obey me.﴾ [Al 'Imran: 50] ﴿Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is a straight path.﴾ [Al 'Imran: 51]

Al-qalam (the pen): well known, and it is that with which one writes. Its plural is aqlam. The word also applies to the lot-arrow with which one casts lots, and it is a verb in the sense of a passive participle, because it is trimmed (yuqallamu), i.e., sharpened and made even. It was said that it is derived from al-qulamah, which is a weak plant because of its thinness. Al-qulamah is also what falls from the fingernail when it is trimmed, and qallamtu azfarahu means I took from them and made them even. Zuhayr said:

*Near a lion, armed, fierce, whose mane is thick, whose claws have not been trimmed.*

And one of the later poets said:

*He is likened to the crescent moon, and that is a deficiency; the paring of his fingernail is like the crescent.*

Al-wahy (revelation): the placing of a meaning into the soul in a hidden manner. It may come through an angel to the messengers, through inspiration as in His saying: ﴿And your Lord inspired the bee﴾ [al-Nahl: 68], through gesture, as in the saying of the poet:

*They conveyed to us, and the fingertips were their messengers.*

And ﴿So he inspired them to glorify (Allah)﴾ [Maryam: 11], and through writing. Zuhayr said:

*Their poems reached the non-Arabs and the horizons, remaining as revelation remains in the deaf stone.*

Al-wahy also means a written book. He said:

*So the streams of al-Rayyan, its traces have been effaced, its emptiness, as its writings preserve them.*

It was said that al-wuhiy is the plural of wahy. As for the verb, it is said awha and wahā.

Al-Masih (the Messiah): a Hebrew word that was Arabized. Its origin in Hebrew is mashiha, with a shin, and it was Arabized with a sin, just as it was changed in Musha, so it became Musa. This is what Abu 'Ubayd said. Al-Zamakhshari said: its meaning is "the blessed," like His saying: ﴿And He made me blessed wherever I may be﴾ [Maryam: 31]. It is among the honourable titles, like al-Siddiq and al-Faruq. End of quote. It was also said that al-Masih is Arabic, and there is disagreement: is it derived from al-siyahah (wandering), so that its pattern is mif'il, or from al-mash (wiping), so that its pattern is fa'il? And does it mean "passive" or "active"? There is a difference of opinion. The reason he was given this name will become clear in the exegesis.

Al-kahl (the middle-aged man): the one who has reached the age of kuhulah, the last of which is sixty. It was also said fifty, and it was said fifty-two. Then he enters the age of old age (shaykhukhah).

There is disagreement about its beginning. It was said thirty, it was said thirty-two, it was said thirty-three, it was said thirty-five, and it was said forty years.

It is from iktahala al-nabat, when the plant became strong and grew high, and from it comes al-kahil (the shoulder-top). Ibn Faris said: iktahala al-rajul and the grey hair covered him, from their saying iktahalat al-rawdah when the blossom covered it. A woman is called kahilah. End of quote.

It is related from the scholars regarding the order of the ages of a child and the changes of his conditions: while in the womb he is janin; when born he is walid; if he does not complete the first week he is sadid; if he continues to nurse he is rada'i; when weaned he is fatim; if he does not nurse he is jahush; when he crawls and grows he is darij; when his milk teeth fall out he is mathghur; when they grow again after falling he is mutaghgbar, with ta' and tha'. When he exceeds ten he is mutara'ri' and nashi'; when he is about to reach puberty he is yafi' and muhriq; when he has a wet dream he is mahzur. In all these states he is a ghulam. When his moustache turns green and his sideburns flow, he is baqil; when he becomes dhaqin (his beard grows), he is fata and sharikh; when his beard is complete he is mujtama'. Then, as long as he is between thirty and forty, he is shabb; then he is kahl until he completes sixty. This is what is well known among the people of lexicography.

Al-tin (clay): well known. It is said tanahu Allahu 'ala kadha, and tamahu, by replacing the nun with a mim, meaning He created and formed him in such a way. Mutayyan is a title of a well-known hadith scholar.

Al-hay'ah (form): the shape and the image. Its origin is a verbal noun. It is said: haa al-shay' yahay'u hay'an and hay'ah, when a thing is arranged and settled into some state. It is transitive by doubling, so you say hayya'tuhu. He said: ﴿And (He) will prepare for you﴾ [al-Kahf: 16].

Al-nafkh (blowing): well known.

Al-ibra' (healing): the removal of illness and disease. It is said: bari'a al-rajul and bara'a min al-maradh (the man was healed of the illness). As for (being free) from sin or from religion, one says bari'.

Al-akmah: blindness that a person is born with, and it may also occur later. It is said kamaha yukimmuhu kamahan, so he is akmah. And kammahtuha: I made her blind. Suwayd said:

*I blinded his eyes until they became white.*

And Ru'bah said:

*She turned away from her, like the turning away of the blind.*

Al-baras: a well-known disease, which is whiteness that afflicts the skin. From it one says baras, so he is abras. The moon is called abras because of its whiteness, and the lizard is a poisonous abras because of the whiteness that covers its skin.

Dhakhara: he dhakharahu, kept it hidden. Al-dhukhr is what is stored. He said:

*For it are the mouse-like rats of meat which it fattens, from the wild cats and a store of its rabbits.*

﴿And when the angels said: "O Mary, indeed Allah has chosen you"﴾: When he had finished the story of Zakariyya, and had digressed from the story of Mary to Zakariyya's, he returned to the story of Mary. This is the usual manner of Arab speech: when they mention something, they digress from it to something else, then return to the first if they have a purpose in returning to it. The aim is to clear Mary of what the Jews accused her of, and to show that it is impossible for Jesus to be a god, so he mentions his birth. The apparent meaning of his words "the angels" is that they are a group of angels. It was also said that what is meant is Gabriel and those with him of the angels, because it is reported that he does not descend for a matter except with a group of angels. It was also said that it was Gabriel alone.

Ibn Mas'ud and Abdullah ibn 'Amr read: "wa-idh qala al-malaikatu" (and the angels said). In the angels' calling her by her name there is reassurance for her and preparation for what they are about to tell her. The object of the verb "said" is the sentence emphasised with inna (indeed).

The apparent meaning is that the angels addressed her directly with speech. Al-Zamakhshari said: It is reported that they spoke to her directly, miraculously, as a sign for Zakariyya, or as a foreshadowing of the prophethood of Jesus. End of quote. By "foreshadowing" he means a precursor and an indication of the prophethood of Jesus. This is the position of the Mu'tazilah, because according to them a supernatural event (khariq li-l-'adah) does not occur at the hand of one who is not a prophet, unless there is a prophet in his time or one is awaited, so that such an event is a preface before the sending of that prophet.

﴿And purified you﴾: purification here means from menstruation, as Ibn 'Abbas said. Al-Suddi said: Mary did not menstruate. Some people said: from menstruation and postpartum bleeding. It is related from Ibn 'Abbas: from the touch of men. And from Mujahid: from whatever blemishes women in form, character, and religion. And from him also: from doubts and suspicions.

﴿and chosen you above the women of the worlds﴾: It was said: He repeated it for emphasis and exaggeration. It was said: there is no emphasis, because by the first choosing is meant the choosing for guardianship, and by the second the choosing for the birth of Jesus, because by his birth she gained additional choosing and a high station above her equals. It was also said: the first choosing is selection, and general, including righteous women; and the second is a choosing above the women of the worlds.

It was said: when the first choosing was stated without restriction, the second clarified that she was chosen above women, not above men. Al-Zamakhshari said: He chose you first when He accepted you from your mother and raised you, and singled you out with a noble honour, and purified you from what is detestable in acts, and from what the Jews accused you of. And He chose you last above the women of the worlds by granting you Jesus without a father, which was not given to any other woman. End of quote. This is a good statement, and "the women of the worlds" is then taken generally. The matter for which she was chosen is her singling out for the birth of Jesus. It was said that it is the service of the house (of worship). It was said: liberation (dedication), and no female was liberated except Mary. It was said: her protection from the prick of Satan. It was said: her prophethood, for it was said that she was made a prophetess, and the angels would appear to her and address her with Allah's message to her, and Zakariyya would hear that, and say: "Indeed, Mary has a great matter." But the majority hold that no woman was made a prophetess. So the meaning for which Mary was chosen above the women of the worlds is something specific to her, so it is a special choosing, since its cause is special. It was said: "the women of the worlds" is specific to the women of the world of her time, so the choosing in that case would be general, as said by Ibn Jurayj.

It is related from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "The best of the women of Paradise is Mary, daughter of 'Imran." It is also related: "The best of her women is Mary, daughter of 'Imran." It is related: "The best of the women of the worlds are four: Mary, daughter of 'Imran; Asiya, daughter of Muzahim, the wife of Pharaoh; Khadijah, daughter of Khuwaylid; and Fatimah, daughter of Muhammad." It is related: "Khadijah has been preferred over the women of my ummah as Mary has been preferred over the women of the worlds." It is related: "Indeed she is among the perfect women." It is related in the authentic hadiths the preference of Mary over the women of the worlds, and a group of exegetes went to the apparent meaning of this preference. Some of our shaykhs said: What I have seen among those upon whom the scholars have agreed is that they transmit from their teachers that Fatimah is the best of women, both the earlier and the later, because she is a part of the Messenger of Allah.

﴿O Mary, be devoutly obedient to your Lord﴾: There is no disagreement among the exegetes that the one who addressed her with this was the angels mentioned earlier, according to the difference mentioned. By qunut here is meant worship, as said by al-Hasan and Qatadah. Or: prolonged standing in prayer, as said by Mujahid, Ibn Juraij, and al-Rabi'. Or: obedience. Or: sincerity, as said by Ibn Jubayr. In His saying "to your Lord" there is an indication that you should single Him out for worship and dedicate worship to Him. The majority hold what Mujahid said, and it is the most appropriate in meaning to His saying ﴿prostrate yourself and bow﴾. Mujahid related that when she was addressed with this, she stood until her feet swelled. Al-Awza'i said: she stood until blood and pus flowed from her feet. It is also related that birds would land on her head, thinking her an inanimate object, because of her stillness in long standing.

﴿prostrate yourself, and bow with those who bow﴾: The angels commanded her to perform three of the postures of prayer. If the apparent postures are meant, then they are conjoined with "and" (wa), and "wa" does not indicate order. So one would only ask why prostration was placed before bowing from the perspective of rhetoric (ilm al-bayan). The answer: since prostration is the posture in which the servant is nearest to Allah, it was given precedence, even though in action it comes after bowing. Thus the precedence is one of honour. It was said that prostration came before bowing in the law of Zakariyya and others among them, mentioned by Abu Musa al-Dimashqi. It was said: in all religions except the religion of Islam, so the precedence came from the order of occurrence in that law, and the precedence in that case is temporal from the perspective of occurrence. This precedence is one of the five types mentioned by the rhetoricians (al-bayaniyyun), and so is the precedence that precedes it. Al-Zamakhshari and Ibn 'Atiyyah agreed that the apparent postures are not what is meant.

Al-Zamakhshari said: She was commanded to perform prayer, and qunut and sujud were mentioned because they are among the forms and pillars of prayer. Then it was said to her, ﴿And bow with those who bow﴾. The meaning is: let your prayer be with the worshippers, that is, in congregation. That is, join yourself to the body of worshippers, be with them and among their number, and do not be among the number of others.

Ibn 'Atiyya said: In my view, Maryam was commanded with two actions and two of the markers (ma'alim) of prayer, namely prolonged standing (qiyam) and prostration (sujud). These two were singled out for mention because of their status among the pillars of prayer. These two apply to her prayer when performed alone. Otherwise, one who prays behind an imam is not told, "Prolong your standing." Afterwards she was commanded to pray in congregation, and it was said to her, ﴿And bow with those who bow﴾. Here another marker of prayer is intended, so that a word is not repeated. The verse does not refer to the sujud and ruku' that are contained within a single rak'ah. The end of his words.

There is no necessity to take the wording out of its apparent meaning.

We have mentioned a reason for placing sujud before ruku'. Ibn 'Atiyya found this problematic and said: This verse is more problematic than our saying, "Zayd and 'Amr stood up," because the standing of Zayd and 'Amr has no known order, whereas it is known that sujud comes after ruku'. How then does the conjunction (waw) come in the reverse order in this verse? The end of his words.

This is the speech of one who has not looked carefully into the book of Sibawayh. Sibawayh mentioned that the conjunctive waw in coordination may carry the sense of togetherness (ma'iyyah), and that mentioning the earlier before the later, or the later before the earlier, are equally possible. Neither of the two possibilities is preferred over the other. No attention is to be paid to the view of some of our later companions who preferred togetherness over mentioning the earlier first, or over mentioning the later first, or who preferred mentioning the earlier over the later.

Al-Zamakhshari gave another explanation for placing ruku' after sujud. He said: It is possible that in her time there were those who would stand and prostrate in their prayer but would not bow, and there were those who would bow. So she was commanded to bow with those who bow, and not to be with those who do not bow. The end of his words. It is as if it was said: Do not limit yourself to standing and prostration, but add ruku' to that.

It was also said: What is meant by "qunti" is "obey," and by "usjudi" is "pray." From this is the verse ﴿And at the adbar of the prostrations﴾ [Qaf: 40], meaning the prayers. By "irka'i" is meant "give thanks with those who give thanks." From this is the verse ﴿And he fell down bowing and turned in repentance﴾ [Sad: 24]. This meaning is strengthened, and it refutes the claim of one who thinks that no prayer was legislated except that ruku' in it precedes sujud. The observed prayer of the Jews and Christians is free of ruku'. It is unlikely that ruku' means the bending that leads to sujud. It is also possible that the omission of ruku' is among what the Jews and Christians changed from the markers of their law.

In His words ﴿with those who bow﴾, the word ma'a (with) implies companionship and joint performance of ruku' together with those who bow, so she would be commanded to pray in congregation. It is also possible that ma'a is used figuratively, so it denotes only agreement in the action without actual joint performance, meaning: act as they act, even if you do not perform the prayer with them, for she used to pray in her sanctuary (mihrab). The phrase is ﴿with those who bow﴾ and not ﴿with those who bow (feminine)﴾, because this plural form is more general, as it includes men and women by way of taghlib (the masculine being used to include the feminine). It also fits the endings of the verses before and after it. And because following men is more excellent, if we say she was commanded to pray in congregation.

Al-Maturidi said: Praying in congregation was not disliked for her, even though she was young, because they were her relatives and kin, and for this reason they were specially entrusted with her care and custody. The end of his words.

﴿That is among the reports of the unseen which We reveal to you﴾ [Al 'Imran: 44]. The reference (dhalika) is to what preceded of the stories of the wife of 'Imran, her daughter Maryam, Zakariyya, and Yahya. The meaning is that the arrival of these stories to you is by way of revelation, since you were not one who studied the scriptures, nor did you accompany anyone who knew such things, and you are from an unlettered people. So the means of knowing this is only revelation from God, as He said in the other verse. He also mentioned the story of the person most distant in time from the time of the Prophet (ﷺ), namely Nuh, peace be upon him, and He gave it in full in Surah Hud more than in other places: ﴿These are among the reports of the unseen which We reveal to you. Neither you nor your people knew them before this﴾ [Hud: 49]. In this is proof of the prophethood of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), since he reported unseen matters that no one could know except one who witnessed them, or one who read them in earlier scriptures, or one to whom God revealed them. Since direct witnessing and reading are excluded, the third possibility is determined, which is revelation from God Most High.

The kaf in dhalika and ilayka is an address to the Prophet (ﷺ). The better parsing (i'rab) is that dhalika is the subject (mubtada'), and "min anba' al-ghayb" (among the reports of the unseen) is its predicate (khabar). Another option is that nuhihi is a new independent clause (jumlah mustaanifah), and the pronoun in nuhihi refers to al-ghayb, meaning: Our practice is that We reveal the unseen to you and inform you of it. For this reason the present tense is used. This is more beneficial than taking it as referring to dhalika, since it includes the stories mentioned and others that He will reveal to him in the future. It becomes like the expression "Zayd feeds the poor," which indicates a continuous state. The form used for this meaning is indeed the present tense. Whereas if it refers to dhalika, it would necessarily mean that nuhihi is in the sense of awhaynahu ilayka (We revealed it to you), since the revelation of it has already occurred and concluded. Then it would be further removed from metaphor than if it included these stories and others that will come later. They also allowed that nuhihi could be the predicate of dhalika, with min anba' being a circumstantial phrase (hal) from the ha' in nuhihi, or being related to nuhihi.

﴿And you were not with them when they cast their pens, [to see] which of them would take charge of Maryam﴾ [Al 'Imran: 44]. This is an affirmation and confirmation that what he knew of this was only through revelation from God Most High. What is being informed about is two stories: the story of Maryam and the story of Zakariyya. He drew attention to the story of Maryam, since it is the primary subject of the report, while the story of Zakariyya came incidentally, as part of it is included in the mention of who would take charge of her. So there is no omission of a reference to one of the stories.

The meaning of ﴿And you were not with them﴾ [Al 'Imran: 44] is: you were not present with them in their presence when they cast their pens. Direct witnessing is negated, although it is already negated by knowledge. The negation does not extend to reading and receiving from the preservers of reports. This is by way of mockery toward those who deny revelation, since they know that he was not one who reads or transmits from the memorizers of reports. Therefore it is determined that his knowledge of this came by revelation from God Most High to him. A parallel to this in the story of Musa is: ﴿And you were not on the western side﴾ [Al-Qasas: 44], ﴿And you were not on the side of Mount Tur﴾ [Al-Qasas: 46]. And in the story of Yusuf: ﴿And you were not with them when they agreed upon their plan﴾ [Yusuf: 102].

The pronoun in ladayhim refers not to something previously mentioned but to what the meaning indicates, that is: you were not with the disputants, like His words ﴿and raised thereby a cloud of dust﴾ [Al-'Adiyat: 4], meaning: by the place. The governing element (al-'amil) of idh is the governing element of ladayhim. Abu 'Ali al-Farisi said: The governing element of idh is "kunta" (you were). The end of his words. This does not fit his view on the incomplete kana (kana al-naqisah), since he holds that it has removed the indication of an event and become purely temporal, and what is of this nature cannot govern a time adverb, because the time adverb is a container for an event, and where there is no event it cannot govern. The present tense after idh has the sense of the past, meaning: when they cast their pens for drawing lots over Maryam. The apparent meaning is that these are the pens used for writing. It was said: They used to write the Torah with them, so they chose them for the lottery seeking blessing through them. It was also said: The "aqlam" here means the "azlam," which are arrows used for divination (al-qidah). Casting here means throwing and dropping. The verse does not mention into what they cast them, nor the manner of the casting, nor how Zakariyya's pen came out. We have mentioned previously some of what the exegetes said about this, and God knows best which of these is correct. Abu Muslim said: The nations used to write their names on arrows during disputes, and whoever's arrow came out was given the matter. This is similar to the arrows by which the slaughtered camel is divided.

﴿Which of them would take charge of Maryam﴾ [Al 'Imran: 44] is in the nominative case as the subject (mubtada'), and its predicate is in a place of accusative (nasb) either by way of quoting a verb of saying that is omitted, meaning: they say, "Which of them will take charge?" The omitted element is indicated by ﴿they cast their pens﴾ [Al 'Imran: 44]. This verse has been cited as evidence for the validity of the lottery (qur'ah), which is a legal question discussed in the science of jurisprudence (fiqh).

Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 3, verses 44–46 (part 1 of 2):

﴿And you were not with them when they disputed﴾: That is, concerning Maryam. It is possible that this dispute was the casting of lots, and that it was another dispute after it. The intent is the intensity of their desire to take charge of her affairs. The governing element of ﴿إذْ﴾ (idh, "when") is the element governing ﴿لَدَيْهِمْ﴾ (ladayhim, "with them"), or ﴿كُنْتَ﴾ (kunta, "you were"), according to the view of Abu 'Ali (al-Farisi) regarding ﴿إذْ يُلْقُونَ﴾ (idh yulqun, "when they cast"). This verse contains, among the kinds of eloquence, repetition in ﴿اصْطَفاكِ﴾ (isṭafāki, "has chosen you"), in ﴿يا مَرْيَمُ﴾ (Yā Maryam, "O Maryam"), and in ﴿ما كُنْتَ لَدَيْهِمْ﴾ (mā kunta ladayhim, "you were not with them"). It was said that there is also inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir, the placing of a word earlier or later than its expected order) in ﴿واسْجُدِي وارْكَعِي﴾ (wasjudī warka'ī, "prostrate and bow"), according to some opinions. There is also metaphor (isti'ara), according to those who held that ﴿القُنُوتَ والسُّجُودَ والرُّكُوعَ﴾ (al-qunut, al-sujud, al-ruku', "devotion, prostration, and bowing") are not a metonymy (kinaya) for the postures of prayer. The allusion to that is among the reports of the unseen. There is generality intended as specificity in ﴿نِساءِ العالَمِينَ﴾ (nisa' al-'alamin, "the women of the worlds"), according to one of the two interpretations. There is simile in ﴿أقْلامِهِمْ﴾ (aqlamahum, "their pens"), if we say he meant the arrows (al-qidah). There is ellipsis in several places.

﴿When the angels said: O Maryam, indeed Allah gives you good tidings of a word from Him﴾: The governing element of ﴿إذا﴾ (idh) is ﴿اذْكُرْ﴾ (udhkur, "remember"), or ﴿يَخْتَصِمُونَ﴾ (yakhtasimun, "they dispute"), or ﴿إذْ﴾ (idh) is a substitute (badal) for ﴿إذْ﴾ in His saying ﴿إذْ يَخْتَصِمُونَ﴾, or for ﴿وإذْ قالَتِ المَلائِكَةُ﴾. These are opinions. The two middle opinions require that the time of the dispute and the time of the angels' speech be the same, and this is far-fetched; it is the opinion of al-Zajjaj. The fourth is distant because of the long separation between the substitute and what it substitutes. The fourth is the choice of al-Zamakhshari, and with it he began. The disagreement concerning ﴿المَلائِكَةُ﴾ (al-malā'ika, "the angels") is whether they are a group of angels, or Jibril alone, as was previously mentioned in their address to Zakariyya and to Maryam. The speech of the angels was mentioned before this good tidings, with mention of her selection, her purification by Allah, and the assurance of worship of Him, as a means of gentleness and kindness, so that this would be a preface to this good tidings of this wondrous, extraordinary matter that had not happened to any woman before her, and will not happen to any woman after her: that she would conceive without a male touching her. The occurrence of that extraordinary matter was also, as a provision from Allah for her, a means of comforting her regarding this extraordinary matter.

Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn 'Umar recited: ﴿وإذْ قالَ المَلائِكَةُ﴾ (wa idh qāla al-malā'ika). The ﴿الكَلِمَةُ﴾ (al-kalima, "the word") from Allah is 'Isa, peace be upon him. He was called a word because of his coming into being through the word "Be" (kun), without a father. This was said by Qatada. It was also said: because he was named al-Masih, and he is a word from Allah, that is, from the speech of Allah. It was also said: because of Allah's promise concerning him in His book, the Torah and the previous scriptures. In the Torah: "Allah came from Sinai, and shone forth from Sa'ir, and appeared from the mountains of Paran." Sa'ir is the place from which the Messiah was sent. It was also said: because Allah guides by His word. It was also said: because it came in accordance with the word of Jibril, which is: ﴿إنَّما أنا رَسُولُ رَبِّكِ لِأهَبَ لَكِ غُلامًا زَكِيًّا﴾ [Maryam 19:19] ("I am only a messenger of your Lord, to give you a pure boy"), so it came in the attribute that was described. It was also said: Allah named him by this, just as He names whomever He wills among the rest of His creation with whatever names He wills. Based on this, it is a proper noun set for him, in which no suitable aspect is considered. It was also said: the word here does not mean 'Isa; rather the "word" is the angels' good tidings to Maryam about 'Isa. It was also said: it is the good tidings of the Prophet to her.

﴿Whose name is al-Masih, 'Isa son of Maryam﴾: The pronoun in ﴿اسْمُهُ﴾ (ismuhu, "his name") refers to ﴿الكَلِمَةُ﴾ (the word), in the sense: We give you good tidings of one brought into being from Him, or of one existing from Allah. He was named al-Masih (the Messiah) because he was anointed with blessing; this was said by al-Hasan, Sa'id, and Shamir. Or: because of the oil with which the prophets are anointed; he came out of his mother's womb anointed with it, and it is a fragrant oil, such that when a person is anointed with it, it is known that he is a prophet. Or: because of purification from sins. Or: because Jibril wiped him with his wing. Or: because he wiped his feet, for there was no hollow in them, and the hollow (al-akhmas) is that part of the sole of the foot that does not touch the ground. 'Isa had a flat foot with no hollow. The poet said:

*"He spent the night struggling with her, a boy like an arrow-shaft, with firm, thick shins, and a flat foot."*
